ru: легко справляться, легко справиться; проходить, пройти без труда
separable: inseparable — *through* keeps hold of its object: *sailed through the test*, *sailed through it*; never ✗ *sailed the test through*
gloss: To get through a test, a task, or a hard stretch of time easily and with no trouble.
examples: She *sails through* every exam without studying.
The bill *sailed through* the Senate in a day.
He's *sailing through* his first semester.

ru: копить, накопить; откладывать, отложить (деньги)
separable: separable, but it usually stands alone or takes *for*: *saving up for a car*; with an amount both orders work — *saved up $3,000*, *saved it up over a year*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we're saving up*), transitive (*saved up enough for the deposit*)
gloss: To put money aside little by little over time in order to buy something.
examples: They're *saving up* for a trip to Italy.
I *saved up* all summer to buy that bike.
He's *saved up* almost three thousand dollars.
contrast: Plain *save* can mean "rescue" or "keep for later"; *save up* only ever means money piling up over time.

ru: сокращать, сократить; урезать; свёртывать, свернуть (планы, расходы)
separable: separable — *scale back the project*, *scale the project back*, *scale it back*; never ✗ *scale back it*
transitivity: both — transitive (*scaled back production*), intransitive (*the airline scaled back after the crisis*)
gloss: To reduce how big, expensive, or ambitious a plan is.
examples: The city *scaled back* its renovation plans.
We've *scaled back* the guest list to forty.
They're *scaling* the program *back* after the budget cut.

ru: увеличивать, увеличить; наращивать, нарастить (объёмы); расширять, расширить
separable: separable — *scale up production*, *scale production up*, *scale it up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*scaled up production*), intransitive (*the startup is scaling up fast*)
gloss: To make something much bigger, especially to turn a small operation into a large one.
examples: The company is trying to *scale up* without hiring.
They *scaled up* production after the first big order.
We've *scaled* the pilot *up* to twelve schools.

ru: уменьшать, уменьшить; сокращать, сократить (размер, масштаб)
separable: separable — *scale down the model*, *scale the model down*, *scale it down*
gloss: To make something smaller while keeping the same shape or proportions.
examples: The design was *scaled down* to fit the lot.
They're *scaling down* the whole operation.
We *scaled* the drawing *down* by half.
contrast: *scale down* points at physical size, *scale back* at ambition or spending — a model is *scaled down*, a budget is *scaled back*.

ru: отпугивать, отпугнуть; спугивать, спугнуть
separable: separable — *scare off the deer*, *scare the deer off*, and a pronoun must go in the middle: *scare them off*, never ✗ *scare off them*
gloss: To frighten a person or animal into going away, or to make a buyer lose interest.
examples: The dog *scares off* anyone who comes near the gate.
High prices *scared off* most buyers.
You're *scaring* him *off* with all these questions.
contrast: *scare away* means the same thing and behaves the same way; Americans use both.

ru: раздобывать, раздобыть; наскребать, наскрести
separable: separable — *scare up some chairs*, *scare some chairs up*, *scare them up*
gloss: To manage to find or put together something out of whatever happens to be available.
examples: See if you can *scare up* a few more chairs.
He *scared up* enough cash for a bus ticket.
We're *scaring up* volunteers for Saturday.
contrast: Nothing frightening about it: American *scare up* simply means "find with some effort".

ru: уплетать, уплести; жадно съедать, съесть; уминать, умять
separable: separable — *scarf down a sandwich*, *scarf a sandwich down*, *scarf it down*
gloss: To eat something very fast.
examples: He *scarfed down* two slices and ran for the bus.
They *scarf down* whatever's in the fridge.
She's *scarfing* her lunch *down* at her desk.
contrast: The verb takes a plain -s: *he scarfs down lunch*. Only the neck-warmer has the plural *scarves*. Informal American — in writing use *eat quickly*.

ru: расхватывать, расхватать; быстро скупать, скупить
separable: separable — *scoop up the tickets*, *scoop the tickets up*, *scoop them up*
gloss: To buy or take something quickly, before anyone else can get it.
examples: Fans *scooped up* the tickets in an hour.
Investors are *scooping up* cheap houses.
She *scooped* the last two *up* before I got there.

ru: подвигаться, подвинуться; сдвигаться, сдвинуться (освобождая место)
separable: no object — intransitive; nothing ever comes between *scoot* and *over*
gloss: To move a short way sideways so that someone else has room to sit.
examples: Can you *scoot over* a little?
He *scooted over* so she could sit down.
Everyone was *scooting over* to make room for the twins.

ru: разведывать, разведать; присматриваться, присмотреться; осматривать, осмотреть заранее
separable: separable — *scope out the place*, *scope the place out*, *scope it out*
gloss: To look a place or a situation over carefully in advance, to see what it is like.
examples: Let's *scope out* the parking situation first.
We *scoped* the venue *out* last weekend.
He's been *scoping out* colleges all fall.

ru: подыскивать, подыскать; разведывать, разведать
separable: separable — *scout out a campsite*, *scout a campsite out*, *scout it out*
gloss: To search an area in order to find something suitable.
examples: They *scouted out* three possible campsites.
I'll *scout* a route *out* before we drive it.
She's *scouting out* office space downtown.
contrast: *scout out* is about finding one good option; *scope out* is about sizing up a place you already have in mind.

ru: перебиваться, перебиться; еле сводить концы с концами
separable: no object — intransitive; what you live on follows *on*: *scrape by on one paycheck*
gloss: To manage to live or succeed with barely enough money or barely enough ability.
examples: They *scrape by* on one paycheck.
We *scraped by* that first winter.
He's been *scraping by* since the layoff.
contrast: Spelling: *scrape* drops its -e before -ing — *scraping*, not ✗ *scrapeing*.

ru: наскребать, наскрести; с трудом собирать, собрать
separable: separable — *scrape together the rent*, *scrape the rent together*, *scrape it together*
gloss: To manage with difficulty to collect enough money, people, or material.
examples: We *scraped together* enough for the deposit.
She's *scraping together* a team for Saturday.
They *scraped* the money *together* somehow.

ru: отсеивать, отсеять; отфильтровывать, отфильтровать
separable: separable — *screen out spam*, *screen spam out*, *screen it out*
gloss: To remove unwanted people or things by checking them against a standard.
examples: The filter *screens out* most junk mail.
Two rounds of tests *screened out* half the applicants.
They're *screening* the weaker bids *out* first.

ru: портачить, напортачить; портить, испортить; лажать, облажаться
separable: separable — *screw up the order*, *screw the order up*, *screw it up*; very often with no object at all: *I screwed up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*sorry, I screwed up*), transitive (*screwed up the whole schedule*)
gloss: To make a bad mistake, or to ruin something by handling it badly.
examples: I *screwed up* the dates on the invitation.
Don't *screw* this *up*.
He's been *screwing up* at work all month.
contrast: Informal. In writing or with strangers say *mess up* or *make a mistake*; *screw up* is fine with friends, wrong in an interview.

ru: кидать, кинуть; обманывать, обмануть; поступать, поступить подло с
separable: separable, and a pronoun *must* split it: *screwed me over*, never ✗ *screwed over me*; with a noun both orders work — *screwed over his partner*, *screwed his partner over*
gloss: To treat someone very unfairly, usually for your own gain.
examples: The landlord *screwed* them *over* on the deposit.
He *screwed over* everyone who trusted him.
I'm not going to *screw* you *over*.
contrast: Rude and informal — strong enough that it accuses someone, not just criticizes them.

ru: валять дурака; бездельничать; тратить, потратить время впустую
separable: no object — intransitive; what you are fiddling with follows *with*: *screwing around with the settings*
gloss: To waste time instead of doing what you are supposed to be doing.
examples: Quit *screwing around* and finish your homework.
We *screwed around* all afternoon.
He's been *screwing around* with the code instead of fixing the bug.

ru: перекрывать, перекрыть; оцеплять, оцепить; изолировать (участок)
separable: separable — *seal off the street*, *seal the street off*, *seal it off*
gloss: To close an area completely so that nobody can go in or out.
examples: Police *sealed off* the block within minutes.
They're *sealing off* the damaged wing.
The tunnel has been *sealed off* since the flood.

ru: заклинивать, заклинить; заедать, заесть; сводить, свести (о мышце)
separable: no object — intransitive; the engine or the muscle is the subject, and nothing comes between the two words
gloss: Of a machine or a part of the body, to stop moving suddenly and stick.
examples: The engine *seized up* on the highway.
My back *seizes up* every time I lift something heavy.
Credit markets were *seizing up* by October.
contrast: Spelling trap: *seize* breaks the "i before e" rule — *seize*, *seized*, *seizing*, never ✗ *sieze*.

ru: подавать, подать (на стол); преподносить, преподнести
separable: separable — *serve up dinner*, *serve dinner up*, *serve it up*
gloss: To put food in front of people, or to offer an audience something ready-made.
examples: They *serve up* the best pancakes in town.
He *served up* a three-course meal in an hour.
The show is *serving up* the same jokes it did last year.

ru: успокаиваться, успокоиться; утихомириваться, утихомириться
separable: separable when you calm someone else — *settle the kids down*, *settle them down*; most often it takes no object at all: *settle down!*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*settle down, please*), transitive (*settled the class down*)
gloss: To become calm and quiet, or to make someone calm and quiet.
examples: *Settle down*, everyone — the movie's starting.
It took an hour to *settle* the twins *down*.
The wind had *settled down* by evening.

ru: остепеняться, остепениться; обзаводиться, обзавестись домом и семьёй
separable: no object — intransitive; the place follows *in*: *settled down in Austin*
gloss: To begin a quiet, permanent life in one place, usually with a partner and a steady job.
examples: They *settled down* in a small town outside Austin.
He's not ready to *settle down*.
Her parents keep asking when she's *settling down*.
contrast: One verb, two lives: a noisy classroom *settles down*, and so does a thirty-year-old who marries and buys a house. Only the subject tells you which.

ru: обживаться, обжиться; осваиваться, освоиться (на новом месте)
separable: no object — intransitive; the place takes *at* or *in*: *settling in at the new office*
gloss: To get used to a new home, job, or school and start feeling comfortable there.
examples: Give her a week to *settle in*.
We *settled in* faster than we expected.
He's still *settling in* at the new school.
contrast: Spelling: *settle* drops its -e before -ing — *settling*, not ✗ *settleing*.

ru: рассчитываться, рассчитаться; расплачиваться, расплатиться
separable: no object — intransitive; the person you owe follows *with*: *settle up with the waiter*
gloss: To pay what you owe so that nobody owes anybody anything.
examples: Let's *settle up* before you leave.
We *settled up* at the end of the trip.
He's *settling up* with the contractor now.

ru: довольствоваться, удовольствоваться; соглашаться, согласиться на (меньшее)
separable: inseparable — *for* holds its object: *settled for second place*, *settled for it*; never ✗ *settled second place for*
gloss: To accept something less than what you wanted, because nothing better is on offer.
examples: We wanted a house, but we *settled for* a condo.
Don't *settle for* the first offer you get.
She's not *settling for* anything less than the lead role.

ru: останавливаться, остановиться на; выбирать, выбрать окончательно
separable: inseparable — *settled on a name*, *settled on it*; never ✗ *settled a name on*
gloss: To make a final choice among several possibilities.
examples: They *settled on* the blue one in the end.
We've *settled on* a date for the wedding.
He's *settling on* a major this semester.
contrast: *settle on* is a free choice among good options; *settle for* is giving in and taking less.

ru: исправляться, исправиться; браться, взяться за ум; подтягиваться, подтянуться
separable: no object — intransitive; the two words never come apart
gloss: To start behaving or performing better.
examples: You'd better *shape up* or you'll be off the team.
He *shaped up* fast once the coach benched him.
The whole department is finally *shaping up*.
contrast: The full American saying is *shape up or ship out* — improve, or leave.

ru: складываться, сложиться; вырисовываться, вырисоваться
separable: no object — intransitive; usually followed by an adverb or by *to be*: *shaping up nicely*, *shaping up to be a long night*
gloss: To develop in a particular way, usually a promising one.
examples: The season is *shaping up* to be a good one.
Plans *shaped up* quickly after the meeting.
How is the new hire *shaping up*?

ru: сбривать, сбрить; скидывать, скинуть (время, цену)
separable: separable — *shave off twenty minutes*, *shave twenty minutes off*, *shave it off*
gloss: To cut a small amount off a time, a price, or a piece of material — or hair off a face.
examples: The new route *shaves off* twenty minutes.
He *shaved off* his beard on a dare.
They're *shaving* a few dollars *off* the price.
contrast: *shaven* survives only as an adjective (*a clean-shaven face*); the verb's past and participle are both *shaved*.

ru: раскошеливаться, раскошелиться; выкладывать, выложить (деньги)
separable: separable with an amount — *shell out $200*, *shell it out*; with no amount it takes *for*: *shelled out for new tires*
transitivity: both — transitive (*shelled out four hundred bucks*), intransitive (*we shelled out for the good seats*)
gloss: To pay a lot of money for something, usually unwillingly.
examples: We *shelled out* almost a thousand dollars for the repair.
Fans are *shelling out* $300 a ticket.
He's *shelled out* more than he can afford.

ru: отправлять, отправить (кого-л. куда-л.); спроваживать, спровадить
separable: separable — *ship the kids off to camp*, *ship off the kids*, *ship them off*
gloss: To send someone away to a distant place, often whether they want to go or not.
examples: They *shipped* him *off* to boarding school.
Her parents *ship* her *off* to her grandmother's every July.
New recruits are being *shipped off* next week.
contrast: Spelling: *ship* doubles the p — *shipped*, *shipping*.

ru: отбывать, отбыть; отправляться, отправиться; отгружать, отгрузить
separable: separable when goods are the object — *ship out the orders*, *ship them out*; with no object it means "leave": *we ship out Monday*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*his unit ships out at dawn*), transitive (*they shipped out 400 units*)
gloss: To leave for a distant posting, especially in the military, or to send goods away to customers.
examples: His battalion *ships out* on Sunday.
We *shipped out* the last of the orders yesterday.
They're *shipping out* two hundred boxes a day.

ru: приценяться, прицениться; искать, поискать, где дешевле
separable: no object — intransitive; what you are looking for follows *for*: *shop around for insurance*
gloss: To compare prices or offers at several places before you buy.
examples: *Shop around* before you sign anything.
We *shopped around* and saved two hundred dollars.
She's *shopping around* for a better rate.
contrast: Spelling: *shop* doubles the p — *shopped*, *shopping*.

ru: подкреплять, подкрепить; укреплять, укрепить; поддерживать, поддержать
separable: separable — *shore up the economy*, *shore the economy up*, *shore it up*
gloss: To support something that is weak or failing so that it does not collapse.
examples: The loan *shored up* the company for another year.
They're *shoring up* the bridge before winter.
The mayor has *shored up* support among older voters.

ru: перекрикивать, перекричать; заглушать, заглушить криками
separable: separable — *shout down the speaker*, *shout the speaker down*, *shout her down*
gloss: To stop someone from being heard by shouting louder than they can speak.
examples: Protesters *shouted down* the mayor.
He was *shouted down* before he finished his first sentence.
They're *shouting* him *down* again.

ru: выкрикивать, выкрикнуть; громко называть, назвать
separable: separable — *shout out the answer*, *shout the answer out*, *shout it out*; also used with no object: *just shout out if you need help*
transitivity: both — transitive (*shouted out the numbers*), intransitive (*shout out if you can't hear*)
gloss: To say something loudly so that everyone can hear it.
examples: Kids were *shouting out* answers before she finished the question.
Someone *shouted out* my name in the crowd.
*Shout out* if you can't hear me in the back.
contrast: The noun *a shout-out* is a public thank-you: *a shout-out to my parents*. It is hyphenated; the verb is two words.

ru: отмахиваться, отмахнуться от; не придавать, не придать значения
separable: separable — *shrug off the criticism*, *shrug the criticism off*, *shrug it off*
gloss: To treat something unpleasant as unimportant and pay no attention to it.
examples: He *shrugged off* the insult and kept walking.
She *shrugs off* every bad review.
The team is *shrugging* the loss *off*.
contrast: Spelling: *shrug* doubles the g — *shrugged*, *shrugging*.

ru: избегать, избежать; уклоняться, уклониться от; сторониться
separable: inseparable — the thing avoided always sits after *from*: *shy away from conflict*, *shy away from it*; never ✗ *shy conflict away from*
gloss: To avoid something because it makes you uneasy or afraid.
examples: He *shies away from* anything that looks like paperwork.
She never *shied away from* a hard question.
Investors are *shying away from* the whole sector.
contrast: Spelling: -y becomes -ie before -s and -ed — *shies*, *shied* — but stays before -ing: *shying*.

ru: принимать, принять сторону; становиться, стать на сторону
separable: inseparable — *with* keeps its object: *sided with her brother*, *sided with him*; never ✗ *sided her brother with*
gloss: To support one person or group in an argument or dispute.
examples: The court *sided with* the tenants.
My mom always *sided with* my sister.
Two senators are *siding with* the governor on this.

ru: перебирать, перебрать; просматривать, просмотреть (в поисках чего-л.)
separable: inseparable — *through* keeps its object: *sifting through the files*, *sifting through them*; never ✗ *sift the files through*
gloss: To go through a large amount of material piece by piece in order to find something.
examples: Investigators *sifted through* hours of video.
I'm *sifting through* a box of old photos.
She has *sifted through* every résumé twice.

ru: записываться, записаться; регистрироваться, зарегистрироваться
separable: separable when you enroll someone else — *sign up the whole class*, *sign them up*; with yourself it takes no object, and what you join follows *for*: *signed up for Spanish*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*I signed up yesterday*), transitive (*she signed the kids up*)
gloss: To put your name on a list in order to join a class, a service, or an activity.
examples: Forty people *signed up* in the first hour.
*Sign up* before Friday if you want a spot.
He's *signing* his daughter *up* for swim lessons.
contrast: The g in *sign* is silent — /saɪn/, not ✗ /sɪɡn/ — though it comes back in *signature*.

ru: регистрироваться, зарегистрироваться (по прибытии); входить, войти в систему
separable: separable when you register someone else — *sign in a visitor*, *sign him in*; about yourself it takes no object: *sign in at the front desk*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*please sign in*), transitive (*I signed my guest in*)
gloss: To write your name on arrival, or to enter your username and password to get into an account.
examples: Visitors have to *sign in* at the front desk.
I *signed in* with my work email.
She's *signing* her guest *in* now.
contrast: *log in* is the everyday synonym online; *sign in* is what the buttons on American websites usually say.

ru: выходить, выйти из системы; отмечаться, отметиться при уходе; брать, взять под расписку
separable: separable when equipment is the object — *sign out a laptop*, *sign it out*; about yourself it takes no object: *sign out before you leave*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*don't forget to sign out*), transitive (*he signed out a camera*)
gloss: To record that you are leaving, to leave an online account, or to borrow equipment by signing for it.
examples: Please *sign out* at the desk on your way past.
I *signed out* of my account on that computer.
He's *signing* a camera *out* for the weekend.

ru: заканчивать, закончить (передачу, письмо); прощаться, попрощаться
separable: no object — intransitive; nothing comes between the two words
gloss: To end a broadcast, a letter, or an online session.
examples: The station *signs off* at midnight.
She *signed off* with "talk soon".
I'm *signing off* for the night.

ru: утверждать, утвердить; давать, дать добро; визировать, завизировать
separable: inseparable — what is approved always follows *on*: *signed off on the budget*, *signed off on it*; never ✗ *signed the budget off on*
gloss: To give official approval to a plan, a document, or a decision.
examples: Legal has to *sign off on* the contract.
Who *signed off on* this design?
She's *signing off on* the final budget today.
contrast: Without *on* it means something else entirely: *sign off* is ending a broadcast, *sign off on* is approving a document.

ru: наниматься, наняться; подписывать, подписать контракт; присоединяться, присоединиться
separable: no object — intransitive; the role follows *as*, the project follows *to* or *for*: *signed on as a consultant*, *signed on to the project*
gloss: To agree formally to join a job, a team, or a project.
examples: Two more sponsors have *signed on*.
He *signed on* as a consultant for six months.
She's *signing on* for another season.

ru: переписывать, переписать (имущество); передавать, передать права на
separable: separable, and a pronoun must split it — *signed it over to his son*, never ✗ *signed over it*; with a noun both orders work: *signed over the deed*, *signed the deed over*
gloss: To transfer property or rights to another person by signing a legal document.
examples: He *signed over* the house to his daughter.
She *signed* the car title *over* last week.
They're *signing* the patents *over* to the university.

ru: отказываться, отказаться от прав (подписав документ); отдавать, отдать по подписи
separable: separable — *sign away your rights*, *sign your rights away*, *sign them away*
gloss: To give up a right or a claim by signing something, usually for good.
examples: Don't *sign away* your right to sue.
He *signed away* his share of the business for almost nothing.
They're being asked to *sign* their privacy *away*.
contrast: *sign over* hands something to a named person; *sign away* stresses what you lose.

ru: остывать, остыть; успокаиваться, успокоиться; утихать, утихнуть
separable: no object — intransitive; the two words never come apart
gloss: To become calm after being angry or excited.
examples: *Simmer down* — nobody's blaming you.
He *simmered down* once he heard the whole story.
The crowd was finally *simmering down*.
contrast: *simmer down* cools an angry person; *settle down* also quiets a noisy or restless one.

ru: выделять, выделить; выбирать, выбрать (одного из многих)
separable: separable, and a pronoun must split it — *singled her out*, never ✗ *singled out her*; with a noun both orders work: *singled out one student*, *singled one student out*
gloss: To choose one person or thing out of a group for special attention, praise, or blame.
examples: The coach *singled out* two players for praise.
Why am I always *singled out*?
She's *singling* him *out* in front of the whole class.

ru: оценивать, оценить; приглядываться, приглядеться к; составлять, составить мнение о
separable: separable — *size up the competition*, *size the competition up*, *size them up*
gloss: To look carefully at a person or situation in order to judge what they are like.
examples: The two dogs *sized* each other *up*.
He *sized up* the room before he spoke.
She's still *sizing up* the new boss.

ru: набрасывать, набросать; излагать, изложить в общих чертах
separable: separable — *sketch out a plan*, *sketch a plan out*, *sketch it out*
gloss: To describe or draw the main points of something without the details.
examples: He *sketched out* the plan on a napkin.
Let me *sketch* the schedule *out* for you.
They're *sketching out* next year's budget.

ru: бегло просматривать, просмотреть; пробегать, пробежать глазами
separable: inseparable — *through* keeps its object: *skimmed through the report*, *skimmed through it*; never ✗ *skim the report through*
gloss: To read something quickly to get the general idea, without reading every word.
examples: I only *skimmed through* the contract.
She *skims through* the news at breakfast.
He's *skimming through* the chapter on the bus.
contrast: Spelling: *skim* doubles the m — *skimmed*, *skimming*.

ru: экономить, сэкономить на; скупиться, поскупиться на
separable: inseparable — *on* keeps its object: *skimped on the details*, *skimped on them*; never ✗ *skimped the details on*
gloss: To spend too little money, time, or effort on something.
examples: Don't *skimp on* the insulation.
They *skimped on* materials and it shows.
He's been *skimping on* sleep all week.

ru: сбегать, сбежать от; увиливать, увильнуть от; бросать, бросить
separable: inseparable — all three words stay together: *skipped out on the bill*, *skipped out on him*; never ✗ *skipped the bill out on*
gloss: To leave without doing something you were supposed to do, or without paying.
examples: They *skipped out on* the check.
He *skipped out on* his family years ago.
She's *skipping out on* practice again.
contrast: Spelling: *skip* doubles the p — *skipped*, *skipping*.

ru: пропускать, пропустить; обходить, обойти (стороной)
separable: inseparable — the object follows *over*: *skip over the boring part*, *skip over it*; never ✗ *skip it over*
gloss: To leave something out, going straight past it to the next thing.
examples: *Skip over* the first two chapters.
He *skipped over* the part where he lost the money.
They're *skipping over* the details for now.
contrast: When people are the object, *skip over* means passed for promotion: *she was skipped over twice*.

ru: обходить, обойти стороной; уходить, уйти от (темы)
separable: inseparable — the topic follows *around*: *skirted around the question*, *skirted around it*; never ✗ *skirted the question around*
gloss: To avoid dealing with a difficult subject directly.
examples: He *skirted around* the question about money.
They've *skirted around* the real problem for months.
She's *skirting around* the subject of her divorce.

ru: халтурить, расслабляться, расслабиться; работать спустя рукава
separable: no object — intransitive; what you neglect follows *on*: *slacking off on the reading*
gloss: To start putting less effort into work than you should.
examples: Don't *slack off* in the last week.
He *slacked off* after the midterm and it showed.
Sales have been *slacking off* since spring.

ru: вкалывать, горбатиться; работать не покладая рук
separable: no object — intransitive; the work follows *at* or *over*: *slaving away at a report*, *slaving away over a hot stove*
gloss: To work very hard for a long time, usually with little reward.
examples: She *slaves away* at that office six days a week.
We *slaved away* all weekend on the yard.
He's *slaving away* over a hot stove.

ru: худеть, похудеть; сокращать, сократить (штат, объём)
separable: separable when something is trimmed — *slim down the menu*, *slim the menu down*, *slim it down*; about a person it takes no object: *he's slimmed down*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*she's slimmed down a lot*), transitive (*they slimmed down the staff*)
gloss: To lose weight, or to make an organization or a list smaller.
examples: He *slimmed down* forty pounds in a year.
The company is *slimming down* its product line.
We've *slimmed* the agenda *down* to four items.
contrast: Spelling: *slim* doubles the m — *slimmed*, *slimming*.

ru: ошибаться, ошибиться; допускать, допустить оплошность; оплошать
separable: no object — intransitive; what you got wrong follows *on*: *slipped up on the dates*
gloss: To make a small careless mistake.
examples: I *slipped up* and called him by the wrong name.
Everybody *slips up* once in a while.
They're *slipping up* on the small details.
contrast: Spelling: *slip* doubles the p — *slipped*, *slipping*.

ru: ускользать, ускользнуть; незаметно уходить, уйти; утекать, утечь (о времени, шансе)
separable: no object — intransitive; the two words never come apart
gloss: To leave quietly without being noticed, or, of time or a chance, to disappear gradually.
examples: He *slipped away* before the speeches started.
Our lead is *slipping away*.
The afternoon had *slipped away* before we knew it.

ru: выскальзывать, выскользнуть; вырываться, вырваться (о словах)
separable: no object — intransitive; the secret or the speaker is the subject: *it just slipped out*
gloss: To leave a place quietly, or, of words, to be said by accident.
examples: I'm going to *slip out* for a minute.
I didn't mean to tell her — it just *slipped out*.
He *slipped out* the back while everyone was eating.

ru: быстро надевать, надеть; накидывать, накинуть
separable: separable — *slip on your shoes*, *slip your shoes on*, *slip them on*
gloss: To put a piece of clothing on quickly and easily.
examples: *Slip on* your shoes — we're late.
She *slipped* a jacket *on* and ran out.
He was *slipping on* his coat when the phone rang.
contrast: Don't confuse it with *slip on* meaning "lose your footing": *she slipped on the ice*. There the *on* belongs to the ice, not to the verb.

ru: замедлять, замедлить; сбавлять, сбавить скорость; притормаживать, притормозить
separable: separable when something is slowed — *slow down the car*, *slow the car down*, *slow it down*; with no object it describes the subject: *the train slowed down*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*the traffic slowed down*), transitive (*the rain slowed us down*)
gloss: To move or happen more slowly, or to make something move or happen more slowly.
examples: *Slow down* — there's a school zone ahead.
The storm *slowed* us *down* by two hours.
Hiring has been *slowing down* since June.

ru: сбавлять, сбавить обороты; снижать, снизить темп жизни
separable: no object — intransitive in this sense; the person is the subject: *the doctor told him to slow down*
gloss: To live or work at an easier pace, doing less than before.
examples: The doctor told him to *slow down*.
She *slowed down* after her second heart attack.
He's seventy and shows no sign of *slowing down*.
contrast: Same two words, two lives: a car *slows down* on the road, and a person *slows down* in life.
